location.title: Weather for a Location
location.description:
Detected Home Assistant Home location: {ha_location}.

If a Home location is configured, latitude and longitude have been pre-filled from your Home Assistant Home zone; otherwise enter them manually. You may override the values to use a different location. The NWS forecast office for this location is suggested in the next step, then a coastal office for surf data.

office.title: Choose NWS Forecast Office
office.description:
Select the NOAA / NWS forecast office to use for {latitude}, {longitude}. The office NWS names for this location is pre-selected, followed by the nearby coastal offices.

{warning}

surf.title: Choose Surf Forecast Office
surf.description:
Choose the coastal office whose Surf Zone Forecast to add as a NOAA Surf entry, nearest first.{none_note}

Each office lists what it provides. Every one gives rip current risk; water temperature needs a tide station and surf height a buoy, and an office without one doesn't get that entity. "no forecast this week" means NWS hasn't issued one in the last 7 days: some offices only issue them in their summer season.

marine.title: Nearshore Marine Forecast
marine.description: Enter an NWS marine zone ID, for example LMZ741 (Lake Michigan, Wilmette Harbor to Northerly Island). Nearshore marine forecasts come from the Great Lakes offices, for the zones near the shore. The zone's office and name come from NWS, and the forecast is its own NOAA Marine entry.

error.invalid_office: Please choose a valid NWS forecast office.
error.invalid_marine_zone: Enter a marine zone ID such as LMZ741: two letters, Z, then three digits.
error.marine_zone_not_covered: {zone} is not in a nearshore marine forecast. Those cover the Great Lakes zones near the shore; open-lake and ocean zones have other forecasts.
error.marine_forecast_stale: {zone}'s office hasn't issued a nearshore marine forecast in the last 24 hours. Try again later.
error.cannot_connect: Could not reach NWS. Try again in a moment.

abort.already_configured: This NOAA office and location is already configured.
abort.surf_already_configured: Surf data for this office is already set up.
abort.all_surf_configured: Every surf forecast office is already set up.
abort.unknown_surf_office: That office does not issue a Surf Zone Forecast.
abort.already_in_progress: This is already being set up.
abort.marine_already_configured: The marine forecast for this zone is already set up.

init.title: NOAA It All Options
init.description:
Detected Home Assistant Home location: {ha_location}.

Update the latitude and longitude used for NOAA data. The NWS forecast office for this location will be suggested in the next step. Surf forecasts and hurricanes are separate entries: add them with Add entry, or delete them.

office.title: Choose NWS Forecast Office
office.description:
Select the NOAA / NWS forecast office to use for {latitude}, {longitude}. The office NWS names for this location is pre-selected, followed by the nearby coastal offices.

{warning}

radar.title: Radar Loop History
radar.description:
How many hours of radar the animated Radar Loop should cover.

NOAA's own loop is fixed at roughly 50 minutes and it only keeps ten frames on the server, so anything longer is collected here instead: one frame per refresh, saved under your Home Assistant configuration directory and kept across restarts. A newly configured loop starts short and fills out over the hours that follow.

Expect a few megabytes of storage per radar site, and note that the assembled animation is larger than NOAA's, so every open dashboard re-downloads it each time it changes.

Set 0 to serve NOAA's own loop unchanged and store nothing. Maximum {max_hours} hours.

error.invalid_office: Please choose a valid NWS forecast office.
error.invalid_radar_hours: Radar history must be a whole number of hours between 0 and {max_hours}.
